feedback: When the child changes only ramp height and reads the flags: 'You changed just one thing — the height — so you can SEE which ramp wins, not just guess.'
If the child changes two things at once (e.g. swaps the car and raises the ramp): 'Change just one thing, or we won't know what made the difference.'
If the child names the guess instead of the result: 'Show me which flag went furthest — let's answer from what really happened.'
activities.intendedInsight: A test is a way to make the world answer your question: when I change one thing and watch, the result shows me the answer instead of me just guessing.
learnerActions: Start from a real question the child cares about, e.g. 'Which ramp makes the toy car roll the FURTHEST?'
Say your guess first (predict), then set the ramp low, release the car, and mark where it stops with a flag.
Change ONE thing — raise the ramp height — release the same car again, and mark where it stops with a new flag.
Compare the flags and finish the sentence 'The car goes furthest when the ramp is…' by choosing the answer the flags actually show.
If tempted to also swap the car or the floor surface at the same time, change only one thing so you can tell what made the difference.
activities.title: Test Bench: which ramp sends the car furthest?

feedback: If the child gives the car a harder push or a different start on a favourite surface: 'Did each surface get a fair go? What did you change? Let's release it from the same spot each time.'
If the child names the surface they predicted rather than the one that actually won: 'Show me which one really went furthest — let's answer from what we saw.'
If the child narrates the fun ('it went really fast!') without concluding: 'So, which surface lets the car roll the furthest?'
activities.intendedInsight: To compare fairly, release the same car from the same start point the same way (no extra push) and change only the surface — then the answer comes from what you observed, not what you expected.
learnerActions: Set out a ramp, a toy car and three floor surfaces at the bottom of the ramp — carpet, smooth wood, bubble wrap — with the question 'which surface lets the car roll the furthest?'
Release (don't push) the same car from the same spot on the same ramp onto each surface in turn, changing only the surface.
Watch and describe how far the car goes each time (mark or tally the distance).
Keep everything else the same each time so each surface gets a fair go.
Finish by answering the question directly from your own marks, e.g. 'the [surface], because the car rolled furthest on it' (add 'every time' only if you repeated the runs and it won each time).
activities.title: Which surface lets the car roll furthest? (real materials)

feedback: For a 'changed too many things' option: 'If you change two things you won't know which one caused the result.'
When steps are ordered correctly: 'Question first, then test, then watch, then answer — that's the loop.'
activities.intendedInsight: A good test changes one thing, watches the result, and uses that result to answer the question.
learnerActions: Answer a few pictorial checks: 'What should you change to test this?'
Put the steps in order: question → test → observe → answer.
Read an answer off a described result: given what happened, say which thing won.
activities.title: Check the loop (quick review)
